question: Find the area of a triangle formed by (1, 0), (-1, 0), (0, 1).
solution:
**Given:**

Point of triangle are A=(1, 0), B=(-1, 0), C=(0, 1).

**Formula Used:**

Area of isosceles triangle=(btimes h)/(2)

where b= Base of the triangle

h=Height of the triangle

d= sqrt{(x₂-x₁)²-(y₂-y₁)²} 

where d= Distance from one point to other

(x₁, y₁)=Coordinates of one point

(x2, y2)= Coordinates of another point

Pythagorean theorem, h² = a² - b²

**Calculation:**

Distance between A and B= sqrt{(x₂+x₁)²-(y₂+y₁)²}=sqrt{((-1)-1)²+(0-0)²}= sqrt{(-2)²+(0)²}=sqrt{4+0}=2 sq. unit

Distance between B and C= sqrt{(x₂+x₁)²-(y₂+y₁)²}=sqrt{(0-(-1))²+(1-0)²}= sqrt{(1)²+(1)²}=sqrt{1+1}=sqrt2 sq. unit

Distance between C and A= sqrt{(x₂+x₁)²-(y₂+y₁)²}=sqrt{(0-1)²+(1-0)²}= sqrt{(-1)²+(1)²}=sqrt{1+1}=sqrt2 sq. unit

here, The two sides of the triangle are equal which means it is an isosceles triangle

Using the Pythagorean theorem,

Height of the triangle=a²=h²+((b)/(2))² 

⇒ h²=a²-((b)/(2))²=a²-((b)/(2))²=(sqrt2)²-((2)/(2))²=2-1=1 

⇒ h=sqrt1=1 

Area of the isosceles triangle=(btimes h)/(2)=(2times 1)/(2)=1 

**The area of the triangle is 1 sq. unit.**
